permutationLabel: Fulminant CDI (hypotension, ileus, WBC 32, lactate 3.2) after antibiotics
summary: 76-year-old care-home resident after a course of co-amoxiclav: profuse diarrhoea that has now slowed, distension, WBC 32, creatinine 210, lactate 3.2, hypotension. Fulminant CDI: oral (± rectal) vancomycin plus IV metronidazole, early surgical consultation, subtotal colectomy or loop ileostomy with colonic lavage if deteriorating.

inputs.hpi: Care-home resident. Finished a week of co-amoxiclav for a chest infection 5 days ago. Profuse watery diarrhoea for 4 days, now fewer stools but increasingly swollen, tender abdomen, drowsy and confused today. Staff report C. difficile on the unit.

exam.general: Drowsy, confused. T 38.6°C, HR 122, BP 84/50, RR 26.
exam.abdomen: Distended, tympanic, diffusely tender with guarding; bowel sounds quiet.

labs.name: C. difficile GDH / toxin
labs.resultText: GDH positive; toxin A/B EIA positive

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis
imaging.result: Pancolitis with marked wall thickening, accordion sign, colonic dilatation to 7 cm, ascites. No free gas.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Fulminant Clostridioides difficile colitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Fulminant C. difficile colitis with septic shock, colonic dilatation and acute kidney injury. Oral and rectal vancomycin with IV metronidazole; resuscitation; urgent surgical review for subtotal colectomy or diverting loop ileostomy with colonic lavage.

mustInclude.note: IDSA/SHEA 2017: fulminant CDI → vancomycin 500 mg four times daily by mouth (plus rectal if ileus) with IV metronidazole.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a C. difficile disease/protocol (triggers: recent antibiotics, hospital/care-home exposure, toxin-positive result): oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin; fulminant: oral/rectal vancomycin + IV metronidazole, surgical consultation (IDSA/SHEA 2017/2021, WSES 2019). Read a toxin-positive lab result.

guideline.name: IDSA/SHEA clinical practice guidelines for Clostridium difficile infection (2017 update) — fulminant CDI
guideline.section: Fulminant CDI (hypotension/shock, ileus, megacolon): oral/rectal vancomycin + IV metronidazole; surgical management (subtotal colectomy or diverting loop ileostomy with colonic lavage)
guideline.citation: McDonald LC, Gerding DN, Johnson S, et al. Clinical practice guidelines for Clostridium difficile infection in adults and children: 2017 update by the IDSA and SHEA. Clin Infect Dis. 2018;66:e1–e48.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — Clostridioides difficile infection in surgical patients (2019 update)
guideline.section: Surgical patients: early surgical consultation in severe/complicated CDI; indications for colectomy
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Di Bella S, McFarland LV, et al. 2019 update of the WSES guidelines for management of Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile infection in surgical patients. World J Emerg Surg. 2019;14:8.

rationale: Permutation: the must-not-miss infective colitis. The toxin result, CT and antibiotic history are recorded; CDI has no disease in PANE and no protocol, so this checks whether any engine reaches it.
